metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Privacy: no record of viewed photos or their metadata
tasks.description: Nothing about which photos were viewed - or their pixels/metadata - is ever written to disk. The app's existence is fine to record: installation, registry file-associations, and read-only config are all allowed (owner re-scope 2026-06-27). The line is drawn at viewing history and photo data, not at the app being installed.
tasks.details: RE-SCOPED 2026-06-27 (owner, reconfirmed): this guarantee is about CONTENT, not the app's footprint. ALLOWED: the MSI installer's registry writes (ProgID, file associations, folder verb), a Start-menu shortcut, and read-only config (Task 8). FORBIDDEN: any persistent record of what was viewed or the data behind it - no thumbnail DB/cache, no recent-files/MRU of photo paths, no temp files of decoded pixels, no logging of viewed paths. Every runtime cache - the decoded ring + ResidentRing mirror, the decode pool's in-flight buffers + pending_uploads, meta_cache, rotation overrides (Tasks 1/3), the failed set, the transient toast, and on-demand EXIF reads (Task 5) - is RAM-backed and dropped on exit (Task 6). pb-core is pure (no std::fs). DONE 2026-06-27: (1) static audit - the only fs::write/File::create in the tree are in #[cfg(test)] code + the offscreen_png example; every view/cache/decode hot path is read-only (read_dir/fs::read/fs::metadata). (2) no-trace integration test `viewing_a_folder_writes_nothing_to_disk` (pb-app) snapshots a sandbox before/after a real scan+decode+EXIF session and asserts zero files created or modified. (3) guarantee + cache inventory + boundary documented in CLAUDE.md (new 'Privacy guarantee' section). Subtask 3 (opt-in persistence flag) DEFERRED - there is no on-disk cache to gate yet; scaffold it if/when one is added.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration 'no-trace' test: run a view session pointed at a sandbox and assert (via before/after filesystem diff) that NO photo-derived files (thumbnails, caches, MRU lists, decoded-pixel temp files) are created anywhere - the installer/registry are a separate process and out of scope. Static audit: no disk-write APIs on the view/cache hot paths; all caches are RAM-backed types. Document the guarantee and its new boundary in CLAUDE.md.

tasks.title: Esc: immediate close, then clean teardown
tasks.description: Pressing Esc immediately closes the photo and the application, cleaning up after itself once it is no longer visible.
tasks.details: On Esc, hide/close the window FIRST for an instant perceived exit, then run teardown: drop the VRAM ring, the byte LRU, decoded buffers, rotation/zoom overrides, and any metadata - implementing the privacy guarantee (Task 2). No flush-to-disk on exit. Ordering matters: the visual close happens before the heavy frees so quitting always feels instant. Register action quit (Task 8). DONE 2026-06-27: Esc (and WindowEvent::CloseRequested) route to App::begin_exit -> (1) window.set_visible(false) so it vanishes before any heavy free; (2) clear_session_state() drops the RAM-only photo-derived caches (ResidentRing reset, pending_uploads/meta_cache/rotations/failed/current/toast cleared) - no disk flush; (3) event_loop.exit(), after which Drop frees the renderer (VRAM) + joins the decode pool while the window is already gone. No-disk-on-exit is covered by Task 2's no-trace test. Visual instant-close confirmed by boot smoke test; interactive Esc timing is owner-verified (GPU/window behavior, per project norm).

tasks.title: Recursive directory mode (R)
tasks.description: R toggles recursive mode: the playlist spans the current directory plus every subfolder, ordered so a folder's own photos show first, then each subfolder in order, recursively - i.e. roughly full-path order.
tasks.details: When recursive mode is on, the scan walks the whole tree and rebuilds the playlist. ORDERING (confirm with owner): directory-grouped depth-first - within a directory its own images come first (natural/numeric sort so img2 < img10), then descend into each subdirectory in natural order, recursively. This differs subtly from a pure lexicographic full-path sort (where a file 'z.jpg' would sort after a subfolder 'a/'); the grouped traversal matches the owner's 'current dir's photos first, then each subfolder'. REBUILD: the app owns the ordered path list while pb-core Playlist holds count + index, so toggling re-scans, re-sorts, rebuilds Playlist (and its precomputed shuffle for the new length), and keeps the current photo by re-finding its new index. PRIVACY (Task 2): scanning reads directory entries only - no on-disk index is written. Use walkdir; skip unreadable dirs; guard against symlink loops. KEY CONFLICT: 'R' (Shift+R) was assigned to rotate-CCW in Task 1 - recommend recursive=R and moving rotate-CCW to another default (trivial via Task 8); confirm with owner. RESOLVED 2026-06-27 (owner): the recursion toggle is Ctrl+R (NOT R), leaving R/Shift+R for rotate (Task 1); and a folder opened via picker/drag-drop/association is recursive BY DEFAULT (Task 12), so this folder-grouped ordering function is the shared one those folder opens reuse.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the path-ordering function over a synthetic tree: a folder's files precede its subfolders' files, folders appear in natural order, natural (numeric) sort holds within a folder. Test toggle on/off keeps the current photo (index re-found). Edge cases: empty subdirs, non-image files filtered out, unreadable dirs skipped.

tasks.title: ICC color management (in-shader) + wide-gamut & HDR output
tasks.description: Color-manage wide-gamut sources in-shader (3x3 matrix + TRC) so Display-P3 / AdobeRGB / ProPhoto render correctly; then present wide-gamut + HDR to a capable display via an fp16 scRGB swapchain.
tasks.details:
DONE (2026-06-27), grew well beyond the original sRGB-correctness scope into full wide-gamut + HDR OUTPUT. THREE layers:

(1) IN-SHADER ICC CMS — pb_decode::color reduces a source ICC to a shader-ready ColorTransform { 3x3 source-linear->BT.709 matrix, 7-param moxcms TRC, enabled }, carried on DecodedImage::color (default sRGB passthrough). Extracted per backend: JPEG APP2 (zune icc_profile), PNG/TIFF/WebP (image-crate concrete-decoder icc_profile via load_with_icc), JXL rendered_icc, HEIC/AVIF the ISOBMFF `colr` box parsed directly in wic.rs (the MS HEIF decoder returns 0 WIC color contexts — verified) handling `prof`/`rICC` ICC and `nclx` CICP. moxcms (pure Rust, was already transitive). sRGB / ~2.2-gamma-with-sRGB-primaries detected as passthrough (bit-exact). Fixes the oversaturated Display-P3 iPhone HEICs.

(2) fp16 scRGB RENDER PATH — pb-render renders the scene to an Rgba16Float scRGB-linear intermediate (SCENE_WGSL: source->scene-linear, no gamut clamp), then a present pass -> the surface. SDR 8-bit surface: extended-Reinhard tone-map (per-image peak) + sRGB-encode. HDR fp16 surface: copy scene-linear straight through. Overlay composites into the linear intermediate so one present pass serves both.

(3) WIDE-GAMUT + HDR OUTPUT (pure wgpu, NO native D3D12 interop — a DXGI fp16 flip swapchain is always scRGB) — pb_render::display::primary_hdr() (DXGI GetDesc1) detects HDR-on; if so the surface is Rgba16Float (scRGB). HDR AVIF/HEIC (PQ/HLG) decode to fp16 scene-linear via WIC's 128bppRGBAFloat (WIC does the PQ/HLG decode for us), carried through (PixelFormat::Rgba16F). Brightness baked in the scene pass (ColorUniform.scale): SDR content x sdr_white-scale, HDR content x 1.0 (absolute scRGB). Owner-confirmed on a Display-P3/HDR/1000-nit panel: P3 visibly wider than sRGB; HDR images get real highlight headroom.

DEVIATION from the original 'assume sRGB display' plan: full wide-gamut + HDR output shipped. Open tuning (followups): real SDR-white-level via DisplayConfig (200-nit default); WIC scRGB reference-white assumption; per-output (not just primary) HDR detection. macOS port = wgpu Rgba16Float surface + EDR (deferred). Known still-SDR: Radiance HDR / OpenEXR (image-crate, not WIC); CMYK JPEG.
tasks.testStrategy: DONE: pb-decode::color unit tests (sRGB passthrough, Display-P3/AdobeRGB matrix+TRC, CICP nclx, LUT-sRGB detection, garbage->passthrough); wic.rs colr-box byte-fixture tests (prof ICC + nclx, HDR-transfer detection); common::finalize_hdr_scrgb fp16 tests; pb-render golden tests (SDR round-trip bit-exact, enabled-transform curve). Verified on the real corpus via the decode example + offscreen PNG render; on-screen wide-gamut/HDR confirmed visually by the owner (the fp16/HDR swapchain is uncapturable by GDI).

tasks.title: Windows: open photos directly (file-arg, drag-drop, picker, recursive-by-default)
tasks.description: Make PhotoBlaze open photos the way a desktop app should: double-click a photo (a file association launches it with a path), drag photos or folders onto the window, or use the file picker (O). Opening a photo shows its folder flat; opening a folder browses it recursively; Ctrl+R toggles recursion at runtime.
tasks.details: Milestone A of the Windows-integration track - behavior only, plain exe, no packaging (ADR-018/019). All entry points normalize to pb-core::open: a thin app I/O shim classifies args/drops into LaunchInput { Empty | Files | Directory } (one fs::metadata call), then the PURE pb-core::open::plan -> OpenPlan { Source::Scan{roots,recursive} | Source::Explicit(files), Cursor::First | At(path) }. Policy: single file -> scan its folder FLAT, cursor on that file; many files -> exactly those; a directory -> scan RECURSIVELY, cursor first; nothing -> empty state + picker. The fs scan + extension filter stay in the app (pb-core has no I/O); pb-core resolves the cursor index (open::resolve_cursor + Playlist::with_cursor). Add the rfd crate for the native Open dialog (O = open file(s); Shift+O = open folder). Wire winit WindowEvent::DroppedFile/HoveredFile (currently unhandled). Ctrl+R re-scans with the opposite recursion and re-finds the current photo (reuse Task 9's folder-grouped ordering). Embed an app .ico + version info via a winres/embed-resource build script so the taskbar/Explorer/association icon is real. CURRENT entry point (main.rs) only accepts a directory and read_dir's it, so a double-clicked FILE path fails today - this task fixes that. This seam makes the macOS port delivery-only (Task 15). DONE 2026-06-27: all subtasks implemented in pb-app — arg/drop/picker classification via pb_core::open, recursive-by-default folders, Ctrl+R toggle, rfd picker + bare-launch empty state, window+exe icons (build.rs/winresource + decode_bytes window icon). tasks.title: HEIC/AVIF: parallel CPU libheif decode (break the WIC serialization)
tasks.description: Route HEIC/AVIF decode to CPU libheif behind the ImageDecoder seam (A/B vs WIC) so the pool's concurrent workers actually parallelize. WIC's HEVC decoder serializes (~1.7x on 8 threads, measured), capping HEIC at ~8/s no matter the worker count; libheif (no shared GPU session) runs truly parallel -> ~8x -> prefetch full-res AHEAD of the user. Preview-first + on-land sharpen already shipped (ADR-020). Full plan, phasing, and the higher-res-preview spike: docs/heic-decode-plan.md.
tasks.details: See docs/heic-decode-plan.md. Decision: ADR-020 (CPU libheif now; NVDEC deferred — iPhone HEICs are 48-tile HEVC grids that libheif handles free). Phase 0 (OWNER, blocker): install vcpkg + cmake, `vcpkg install libheif` (libde265 + dav1d), set VCPKG_ROOT, decide static/dynamic link (dynamic -> ship DLLs in the MSI, update packaging.md). Phase 1: LibHeifDecoder (libheif-rs/libheif-sys) as an ImageDecoder for HEIC+AVIF, cargo-feature-gated, A/B vs WicDecoder; reuse common::finalize_oriented + the colr/CICP color path; preview via libheif thumbnail. Phase 2: bench concurrent throughput vs WIC over 12 & 48 MP (target >=~50/s). Phase 3 (payoff): widen request_prefetch's `upgrade_item` from displayed-only to the window (current-first) so fulls prefetch AHEAD -> sharp at scroll speed; watch VRAM budget + per-frame churn. Phase 4 (gated): NVDEC (ADR-012) only if 48 MP still lags.

tasks.title: Hold-to-fly acceleration ramp (slow start -> refresh-rate)
tasks.description: While a navigation key is held, accelerate the advance rate over time - starting at a few photos per second for control, ramping up to the display refresh cap over several seconds - instead of jumping straight to full speed after the initial tap delay.
tasks.details: DONE (2026-06-28): shipped as a PURE advance_interval(elapsed, min_rate, ramp_secs, frame_interval) -> Duration in pb-app main.rs - a linear rate ramp from ADVANCE_MIN_RATE=3.0/s up to the refresh rate over ADVANCE_RAMP_SECS=4.0s, floored at frame_interval so refresh stays the hard ceiling - wired into the about_to_wait hold-advance gate (replaced the fixed frame_interval due-check). repeat_elapsed is measured from when the tap delay expired (hold_start + initial_delay), so the ramp RESETS naturally on each fresh hold and on a direction change (held_nav is single-key, so reversing = release+press = a new hold_start). All existing gates preserved: tap = one photo, readiness gating (a miss HOLDS, never skips), self-paced to the newest ready frame. The configurable lower cap (Task 20) waits on the settings dialog (Task 22); until then refresh is the max. Unit tests cover the floor (~1/min_rate at t=0), the exact refresh clamp at/after the ramp, monotonic shrink, and the low-Hz no-ramp case; clippy -D warnings + fmt + 31 pb-app tests green; release built + smoke-tested. Feel is owner-verified (hold-to-fly timing is hands-on, per project norm). ORIGINAL PLAN: Today's hold-to-fly (pb-app main.rs about_to_wait, section 3) had NO ramp: after the initial_delay (~400ms) tap gate, advance is gated only by frame_interval (~1/refresh) + decode readiness, so it jumps straight to the refresh-capped MAX cadence. Add a time-based acceleration that mirrors the existing zoom/pan ramps (ZOOM_MIN_RATE->ZOOM_MAX_RATE over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS; PAN_MIN_SPEED->PAN_MAX_SPEED over PAN_RAMP_SECS, applied in apply_view_holds). While a nav key is held, interpolate the advance rate from a gentle floor (ADVANCE_MIN_RATE, a few photos/sec) up to a ceiling over ADVANCE_RAMP_SECS (a few seconds), measured from hold_start (after the initial delay). The ceiling is min(display refresh, the Task 20 configured cap). Convert the rate to a due interval and advance when now >= last_present + interval AND caught_up (displayed == target). PRESERVE every existing gate: tap = one photo (initial_delay); readiness gating (a miss HOLDS the previous frame, never skips); self-paced advance to the newest ready frame each tick. The ramp only sets the ATTEMPTED cadence - decode throughput still caps the real rate (so on slow folders the ramp is moot, on fast ones it controls feel). Reset the ramp clock on a fresh hold and on a direction change (reversing starts slow again), like zoom/pan reset their *_started on release. Make the core a PURE helper (pb-core, or a pure fn in pb-app): advance_interval(elapsed, min_rate, ceiling_rate, ramp_secs) -> Duration, unit-tested. Perf-neutral: pure arithmetic in about_to_wait; no extra allocation; no change to decode/upload.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the ramp: at elapsed 0 the interval ~= 1/ADVANCE_MIN_RATE; at elapsed >= ramp_secs it clamps to the ceiling interval (never faster than min(refresh, cap)); strictly monotonic (rate rises, interval shrinks) in between; a lower ceiling lowers the cap. Property: the attempted rate never exceeds min(refresh, cap). Manual/perf: hold space / enter / backspace - flies slow then smoothly accelerates to full speed; a tap still advances exactly one photo; reversing restarts slow. Shares the gated-advance invariant: no photo is skipped.

tasks.title: Fix: photo briefly stretches (wrong aspect) during fullscreen<->windowed toggle
tasks.description: When toggling between windowed and borderless-fullscreen (F11 / Alt+Enter / the View menu), the photo momentarily stretches out of aspect ratio for a frame or two before it re-renders correctly. The fit math is right; this is a transition-sequencing artifact and we can do better.
tasks.details: ATTEMPTED then FULLY REVERTED (2026-06-28). The bug is a flip-model resize artifact: during the toggle DWM stretches the previous swapchain buffer to the new window size for ~a frame (our own draws are always correctly letterboxed). Tried, in order: (1) PROACTIVE PRESENT (reconfigure + redraw to the new size in toggle_fullscreen instead of waiting for the async Resized) - reduced but did NOT remove the flash. (2) DWM CLOAK across the transition (cloak -> resize -> render correct frame -> uncloak) - this DID remove the stretch, but regressed two things: (a) the Windows shell stopped auto-hiding the taskbar in fullscreen (its fullscreen-detection fires on the resize event, which now happened while the window was cloaked/hidden, so the shell never registered a fullscreen window), and (b) it added a visible blank 'beat' on the transition. A post-uncloak SWP_FRAMECHANGED re-assert did NOT restore taskbar hiding. NET: two worse problems for one minor cosmetic flash, so ALL of it (cloak + reassert + proactive present) was reverted - toggle_fullscreen is back to the plain resize: taskbar auto-hides correctly, no blank, the minor 1-frame stretch is accepted. PROPER FIX (deferred -> now LOW priority): the artifact needs swapchain control wgpu doesn't expose - either DXGI_SCALING_NONE on the flip swapchain (requires native swapchain creation, not via wgpu) or a synchronous WM_SIZE ResizeBuffers via a window subclass. Both are disproportionate to a 1-frame flash; revisit only if it becomes a real annoyance. Follow-up Task 25 (minimize the cloak gap) is now moot and cancelled. ORIGINAL PLAN: REPRO: toggle_fullscreen (pb-app main.rs) flips decorations + window position + inner size (windowed: 1280x800; borderless-fullscreen: monitor size), and now also adds/removes the native menu bar (which itself resizes the client area). Each of these fires one or more intermediate WindowEvent::Resized. The Resized handler reconfigures the swapchain and re-places the quad via quad_vertices (which IS aspect-preserving / letterboxed), then draws; the crisp decode-to-fit is debounced (resize_settle_at, ~180ms). LIKELY CAUSE: with the flip-model swapchain, during the window-size transition the compositor (DWM) STRETCHES the previously-presented frame to the new client size for a frame before our reconfigure + aspect-correct repaint lands - and/or an intermediate Resized size is drawn before the final size settles. So the brief stretch is a stale/early frame being scaled, not wrong fit math. PLAN: (1) Instrument the toggle to confirm the source (compositor stretch of the prior frame vs. a transient intermediate size we draw). (2) Drive the resize from toggle_fullscreen using the KNOWN target size: reconfigure the swapchain + repaint an aspect-correct, letterboxed frame in the SAME step (don't wait for the async Resized), so no stretched intermediate is ever presented. (3) Consider hiding/freezing the surface across the transition (or matching the resumed() 'render-while-hidden then reveal' trick) so the OS never composites a stretched buffer; coalesce the multiple intermediate Resized events. (4) Keep the debounced decode-to-fit for crispness - this fix is purely about the immediate frame's geometry, not the re-decode. Perf-neutral and must not regress the smooth live-drag resize path. Cross-ref: the menu add/remove resize churn was introduced with the windowed-mode menu bar; ensure that path doesn't add its own stretch.
tasks.testStrategy: The pure fit/quad math (fit_rect / quad_vertices) is already unit-tested and stays aspect-correct at every intermediate size - so add a regression test only where it helps (e.g. assert the drawn quad rect preserves the image aspect at both the windowed and fullscreen sizes, and at a representative intermediate size). The artifact itself is timing/compositor-driven, so the primary check is manual/visual: toggle repeatedly in both directions and confirm NO stretched frame appears; optionally capture frames (offscreen_png render path / PresentMon) to verify. Confirm the live-drag resize and the debounced decode-to-fit are unaffected.

tasks.title: In-app settings/preferences UI (options + hotkey remapping)
tasks.description: A settings window - opened with Ctrl+, and a 'Settings...' menu item - that lets users change options (Blaze tuning, max photos/sec cap, recursive-by-default, default scale mode, etc.) and remap hotkeys to actions, applying live and persisting to config. Built as EGUI IN ITS OWN OS WINDOW (decided). This is the GUI FRONT-END over the config backends; it is the first deliberate user-driven disk write (preferences only - privacy Task 2 explicitly allows config).
tasks.details:
SKELETON SHIPPED (2026-06-28): the egui dialog infra (pb-app dialog.rs - a 2nd winit window + egui-wgpu surface, OS dark/light via ThemePreference::System) + a non-wired Settings form skeleton landed and were verified in dark mode; Ctrl+, opens it. REMAINING: a typed settings.toml model + load / apply-live / save (subtask 2 + 6), the keybinding editor (subtask 4, needs Task 8), wiring the controls to live state, and a 'Settings...' menu item. ORIGINAL PLAN: FRONT-END over the config BACKENDS: Task 8 (central action enum + keymap + TOML) for hotkeys, and settings.rs / Task 20 for options. The UI edits an in-memory config, applies it to the running app live, and persists to the config file(s).

RENDERING (DECIDED 2026-06-28, owner): build the settings form as EGUI IN ITS OWN OS WINDOW (a second winit window + an egui-wgpu surface) - a real movable/titled dialog window. egui gives sliders/spinners/combos/checkboxes and key-capture for free, and ports to macOS. Runs only while open, off the photo hot path. THEME: egui must follow the OS dark/light setting - egui doesn't auto-detect it, so drive ctx visuals (egui::Visuals::dark()/light()) from the detected system theme (winit Window::theme() / the registry AppsUseLightTheme we already read in darkmode.rs) and update on WindowEvent::ThemeChanged, matching the native menu + title bar. (Considered + rejected: a native Win32 dialog - pixel-native but heavy + Windows-only; an in-window egui overlay - simplest but not a separate dialog and it covers the photo. About stays a native TaskDialog - see Task 26.)

HOTKEY REMAP: a 'press a key' capture mode that reads the next physical key and assigns it to the selected action via Task 8's action map; surface conflicts (duplicate key / unknown action) using Task 8's validation; offer reset-to-defaults.

OPTIONS (DECIDED, grouped): BLAZE - acceleration as Start speed (photos/sec floor) + Ramp-up time (secs), mapping to Task 19's ADVANCE_MIN_RATE/ADVANCE_RAMP_SECS; Max photos/sec cap (Task 20) as a SLIDER + type-in field, max = detected monitor refresh; Initial hold delay (the ~400ms tap gate). BROWSING - recursive-by-default (Task 12). DISPLAY - default scale mode (Fit/Fill/Original); letterbox/background color; default windowed/fullscreen (settings.rs, already persisted); (SDR-on-HDR brightness later). KEYBOARD - action remapping (Task 8). SYSTEM - 'Set as default viewer' deep-link (Task 14); open config folder; Reset to defaults (always included).

LIVE APPLY + PERSIST: changes take effect immediately on the running app (e.g. update the Task 19 ramp ceiling) and write to the config file on save/close. PRIVACY (Task 2): config writes are explicitly IN-BOUNDS (preferences only, NEVER photo-derived data) - this is the first deliberate user-config write beyond the fullscreen pref; keep it strictly preferences, write atomically (temp + rename), best-effort (a failed write must never break viewing).

ENTRY: Ctrl+, (DECIDED - mac-like, common on Windows too) opens the settings window; also a 'Settings...' muda menu item (reuse the dispatch). The window owns input while open so hold-to-fly/Blaze is paused; Esc / Save / Cancel to dismiss. The help overlay (Task 7) and menu hints reflect any remaps.

TDD: the config model + serialize/parse + validation (conflict detection, defaults merge, option clamps) are PURE and unit-tested (largely shared with Task 8 + Task 20); the interactive widget layer is the hard-to-test GPU/input shell (manual + minimal golden where feasible). Reuses the existing readiness-gated, self-paced advance engine (pb-app main.rs about_to_wait) - a slideshow is just a timer-driven advance, so a not-ready next slide HOLDS (waits for the decode) rather than skips, exactly like hold-to-fly.

DIRECTION: 'continues in the last navigation direction' needs a new last_nav: Nav field (default Forward), updated on every directional nav (nav_press / advance / the menu dispatch). INTERACTIONS: while a nav key is HELD, hold-to-fly drives and the slideshow timer is suppressed, resuming (timer reset) on release. The event loop must stay ticking while the show is on - extend the about_to_wait ControlFlow::WaitUntil to include the slideshow deadline so it wakes to auto-advance (today it goes idle to ControlFlow::Wait when nothing is pending). tasks.title: HEIC color parity (libheif vs WIC): Sony/Apple re-encoded mid-tone difference
tasks.description: On macOS/Apple-re-encoded HEICs of Sony-originated photos, the libheif decode backend renders ~3.5% darker in the mid-tones than WIC (and Apple/Windows Photos). The shift is uniform across R/G/B (no hue cast) and both backends span the full 0..255 range. Decide the correct rendering and make libheif match it.
tasks.details: Found 2026-06-28 while validating the libheif HEIC backend (see .taskmaster/docs/heic-decode-plan.md SESSION UPDATE). The heic_compare example shows iPhone HEICs are pixel-identical between WIC and libheif (mean <1 level/channel), but Sony-originated HEICs differ by mean ~9-11 levels (3.5-4%), uniform across channels, both spanning 0..255 - so NOT a limited/full-range bug and NOT a matrix/color cast, but a transfer-curve (gamma) interpretation difference. PROVENANCE (the files are misleadingly named): EXIF says SONY / ILCE-7M3 (the A7III) + Adobe Lightroom, and the 42-tile 1024x576 HEVC grid is the macOS HEIF encoder's signature - so these are A7III shots, Lightroom-processed, then re-encoded to HEIC by macOS/Apple Photos (the A7III shoots no HEIF). LIKELY CAUSE: the documented libheif quirk where a file's colr (nclx) box disagrees with the HEVC VUI on the transfer/range flag; libheif trusts the bitstream, WIC follows the colr box (which takes precedence per MIAF). SUSPECTED FIX: set heif_decoding_options.autocorrect_broken_input = 1 (and/or output_image_nclx_profile_passthrough) so libheif honors colr. That needs hand-rolling libheif's VERSIONED decoding_options struct (10 versions deep, incl. a nested heif_color_conversion_options) and verifying the target field lands at the correct offset (sanity-check the version byte; confirm the Sony delta collapses to MATCH). LOW PRIORITY: subtle, no clipping/cast, likely imperceptible while browsing, and 'correct' is debatable without a ground-truth render. CORPUS: 10 Sony DSC*.heic in 'C:\Users\jdlien\Pictures\iCloud Photos\Photos' (plus the Sony in D:\Media\Pictures\test-images). VERIFY: cargo run -q --release --example heic_compare -p pb-decode --features libheif -- <file> (watch the mean delta + per-channel means).
tasks.testStrategy: heic_compare mean RGB delta (WIC vs libheif) drops from ~9-11 to MATCH (<3) on the Sony corpus after enabling the option, while iPhone files stay MATCH (no regression). Sanity-check the decoding_options version byte before trusting the struct offset. If a committed fixture is added, use a synthetic/owned image (privacy), not a user photo.

tasks.title: Minimize the fullscreen-toggle blank gap (cloak transition)
tasks.description: The Task 21 cloak fix removed the stretched flash, but the window now briefly disappears (a blank 'beat') before the new mode shows - most visible entering fullscreen. Investigate where the time goes and shrink that gap so the windowed<->fullscreen transition is imperceptible (or as close as the compositor allows).
tasks.details:
CANCELLED (2026-06-28): obsolete - the DWM-cloak approach that caused this blank gap was reverted (see Task 21), so there is no cloak transition to optimize. If a future stretch fix reintroduces a hidden/transition step, revisit this. ORIGINAL CONTEXT: toggle_fullscreen (pb-app main.rs) cloaks the window (DWM DWMWA_CLOAK), applies decoration/position/size + menu changes, reconfigures the swapchain + renders a correctly-fit frame, then uncloaks. The blank duration = our synchronous toggle work PLUS DWM's cloak->uncloak composition latency. It's worst entering fullscreen: the window grows from 1280x800 to the full monitor (e.g. 7680x2160), so the swapchain AND the fp16 scRGB intermediate reallocate at the larger size and the scene re-renders at full res.

MEASURE FIRST (prime directive - don't guess): instrument the toggle with QPC/tracing and report the split across (a) the SetWindowPos calls (set_decorations / set_outer_position / request_inner_size), (b) surface.configure, (c) the fp16 intermediate texture recreation, (d) scene render + present, and (e) the DWM cloak->uncloak latency itself. NOTE: DWM cloak/uncloak likely imposes a ~1-2 vsync floor regardless of our speed - measure it; if it dominates, shaving our work won't help and we need a perceptual trick instead.

CANDIDATE OPTIMIZATIONS: (a) Collapse the window change into ONE Win32 SetWindowPos (style + position + size, SWP_FRAMECHANGED) instead of winit's three separate calls - fewer intermediate states, possibly no cloak needed if one atomic change doesn't flash. (b) Pre-size/persist the swapchain + fp16 intermediate at the monitor size always (or keep a max-size intermediate), so a fullscreen toggle is a viewport change, not a GPU realloc - trade a little VRAM for a near-instant resize (measure the realloc cost to confirm it's worth it). (c) Order the menu add/remove so it doesn't add a second client-area resize inside the cloak (apply after uncloak if that itself doesn't flash). (d) If DWM latency is the floor: clear to the LETTERBOX color while cloaked so the unavoidable blank matches the app background (continuity) instead of flashing the desktop; or explore a brief two-surface overlap.

ACCEPTANCE: no distortion (already met by Task 21) AND no perceptible blank on either direction (target <= 1 frame, or a background-colored beat rather than a desktop flash). Transition-only code - must stay perf-neutral on the photo hot path and not regress the smooth live-drag resize.
tasks.testStrategy: Instrument + report the before/after time split (SetWindowPos vs surface.configure vs intermediate realloc vs scene/present vs DWM cloak latency); capture the transition (PresentMon / high-speed capture) and count blank frames, aiming for <= 1. Mostly a measurement + GPU/window-timing task, so visual confirmation is owner-side (per project norm). Verify no regression to the photo hot path or the live-drag resize, and that the Task 21 anti-stretch guarantee still holds.

tasks.title: 7-Zip (.7z) archive viewing
tasks.description: Open and browse images inside a .7z like a folder, via the PhotoSource seam. Eager: decompress the whole archive into RAM on open (solid archives have no cheap random access); predict-and-refuse when it won't fit RAM; never extract to disk. STATUS (2026-06-28): the pb-source core + the full pb-app integration (dispatch, async open, RAM budget, structured error dialogs) shipped; in-app password entry (DialogKind::Password, wrong->re-prompt) and launch-path async open also shipped. COMPLETE (2026-06-28): the last three subtasks landed -- #5 measured the eager open on real solid-LZMA2 photo archives (archive_probe example: projection predicts RAM to 1.02-1.26x, transient is a flat ~60-200 MB, ~1 GB/s open) and validated the budget constants from data; #6 added the deterministic over-budget refusal test via a budget-injection seam (seven_z_preflight_within); #7 added the WiX .zip/.7z 'Open with' registration (PhotoBlaze.Archive ProgId, candidate-only). All 8 subtasks done. Live post-install association + a real low-RAM refusal dialog remain owner/CI-side manual checks.
tasks.details: STATUS: pb-source core DONE + committed (SevenZSource eager decode-to-RAM via sevenz-rust2 for_each_entries; seven_z_projected_bytes header pre-flight; try_reserve_exact -> OpenError::OutOfMemory; sorted/filtered entries; container(); 12 tests). sevenz-rust2 0.21 is fully pure Rust (bzip2 = libbz2-rs-sys), no C build risk. REMAINING = the pb-app integration + finishing the source. KEY CONSTRAINT: 7z solid archives put many files in one LZMA2 block, so there is no cheap per-entry random access (unlike zip) -> EAGER decode is mandatory. APP DISPATCH (today ZIP-ONLY -- main integration risk): pb-app imports only ZipSource, is_archive()/picker only know .zip, open_archive() always calls ZipSource::open -> add .7z -> SevenZSource WITHOUT regressing zip. MEMORY MODEL (corrected per review): projected_bytes = resident DECOMPRESSED ENCODED image bytes (the jpeg/etc bytes after 7z decode), NOT decoded RGBA. Real peak ALSO includes transient bytes() clones (SevenZSource::bytes clones the resident Vec per decode), decoder scratch, decode-pool RGBA outputs, pending uploads, and the GPU ring -> the BUDGET MUST keep a margin for these transients, not just the resident sum. BUDGET = a FRACTION of runtime-queried available physical RAM (GlobalMemoryStatusEx().ullAvailPhys behind a cfg(windows) helper) MINUS our reservations (GPU ring ~1.5GB + decode pool 512MB) MINUS a transient margin; NOT a hardcoded ceiling; PB_ARCHIVE_RAM_BUDGET override for tests/power-users (the 96GB dev box never triggers refusal naturally). OOM IS UNCATCHABLE (Rust aborts on alloc failure) so PREDICT-and-REFUSE up front; try_reserve is only a backstop (do NOT force a real alloc failure in tests -- no safe injection point). OPEN-TIME != header sum (review): a solid block may have to decompress/skip huge non-image entries between images, so the image-byte sum predicts RESIDENT RAM, not OPEN TIME; measure open time against total archive/stream shape and keep cancellation. ASYNC OPEN (explicit sequencing): classify path -> synchronous header pre-flight (refuse over-budget instantly, before any spinner) -> spawn an archive-open worker tagged with a generation/job id -> keep the CURRENT photo visible with loading feedback (wait spinner / 'Loading archive...') -> on completion DISCARD stale results whose generation != the latest open request -> rebuild_playlist only if still current -> handle app-exit and a second open arriving while a worker runs. STRUCTURED ERRORS (not Option<Resolved>): distinguish TooLarge{needed,budget} / OutOfMemory / Corrupt (damaged or unsupported codec) / PasswordRequired (encrypted incl. encrypted-header; map sevenz Error::PasswordRequired + MaybeBadPassword) / Empty (no supported images) / Io -> each its own message; a password .7z gets a clear 'password protected, not supported yet' message, NOT a generic corrupt dialog. DIALOG (decided): use the app's egui DialogWindow/DialogKind (dark-aware, consistent with About/Settings; aligns with the in-flight dialog.rs error/warning work + the triangle-exclamation/file-circle-xmark icons) by adding an Error/message DialogKind, NOT rfd::MessageDialog; depends on the dialog.rs work landing. Plain, em-dash-free copy: too-big='You have insufficient memory to open this archive. It needs at least X GB.'; OOM='Ran out of memory while loading this archive.'; corrupt='This archive cannot be opened. It may be damaged or use unsupported compression.'; password='This archive is password protected, which is not supported yet.'. PRIVACY: RAM-only, never sevenz extract-to-disk helpers; the no-trace test extends to .7z. PACKAGING/UX: add .7z to the Open dialog filter AND (optional) the WiX 'Open with' candidate list, but do NOT hijack .7z as the default handler. HUGE-ARCHIVE ESCALATIONS (later, same seam): (a) in-RAM per-block LRU (bounds RAM, keeps no-trace, more code); (b) opt-in extract-and-delete to a temp dir (simplest 'just works' but disk-touching -> needs opt-in + disclosure + clear-on-close + leftover-sweep-on-startup; sanctioned by CLAUDE.md 'on-disk scratch must be opt-in + cleared'). v1 = just refuse and let the user extract it themselves.
tasks.testStrategy: VALIDATION required before marking done: (1) cargo test -p pb-source (incl. the .7z fixture tests + the new encrypted->PasswordRequired case). (2) pb-app: ZIP still works (regression) AND a .7z no-trace test (opening+viewing a .7z writes nothing) using a sevenz-rust2 dev-dependency or a committed tiny .7z fixture. (3) Deterministic over-budget refusal via the PB_ARCHIVE_RAM_BUDGET override; do NOT force a real try_reserve/OOM failure (no safe injection -- cover the backstop by code review + the structured-error path). (4) Manual: open a real photo .7z (decodes + navigates); over-budget override shows the too-big dialog; corrupt archive shows the corrupt dialog; password .7z shows the password message; empty (no-images) archive handled gracefully. (5) MEASUREMENT NOTE: record projected_bytes, peak working-set delta, and open time on a representative solid-LZMA2 photo .7z; use it to set the budget fraction + transient margin.

tasks.description: Add the slideshow slide-duration as a persisted, editable preference in the Settings panel. Today the interval (slideshow.rs / task #23) is RAM-only: it defaults to 4.0s every launch and is only adjustable live via the [ and ] keys, so a preferred duration can't be made to stick and the value isn't visible or discoverable anywhere. This gives it a persisted default plus a visible, hand-editable control.
tasks.details: Owner-requested follow-on to the shipped slideshow (#23), routed through the Settings stream (#22) because it touches settings.rs + the settings dialog/form, which that stream owns (the panel is being reorganized into tabbed sections, so put this control in the appropriate tab). CURRENT STATE: the live interval is App.slideshow.interval (a std::time::Duration), seeded from slideshow::DEFAULT_INTERVAL (4.0s) and clamped to [slideshow::MIN_INTERVAL = 0.5s, slideshow::MAX_INTERVAL = 60s]; the [ and ] keys call Slideshow::adjust(-1 / +1) (0.5s steps, clamped) but the value is RAM-only and resets on exit. GOAL: (1) persist a default so a chosen duration survives a restart; (2) surface + edit it in Settings for discoverability. MODEL: add a field to the typed Settings (settings.rs, serde + toml), e.g. slideshow_interval_secs: f64 with #[serde(default ...)] = 4.0, clamped on load. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the range/default: reuse the slideshow.rs constants/clamp rather than re-hardcoding 0.5/60/4.0 (e.g. make slideshow::clamp_interval pub and convert via Duration::from_secs_f64 then clamp), so the Settings clamp and the [ / ] clamp can never drift apart. STARTUP: seed App.slideshow.interval from the setting where App reads the other prefs into live state (mirror start_speed / ramp_secs / max_advance_rate). APPLY-LIVE + SAVE: editing the control updates App.slideshow.interval immediately (a running slideshow's deadline = last_present + interval, so it recomputes live, exactly like pressing [ or ]) and persists on Save (atomic temp+rename; config writes are allowed per privacy #2). [ / ] SEMANTICS (decision, recommended): keep [ and ] as a live SESSION override that does NOT auto-persist; the Settings panel owns the persisted default. (Optional alternative for the implementing agent: have [ / ] write-through to Settings.slideshow_interval so the last-used value sticks; default to NOT doing this to avoid chatty/surprising disk writes on every keypress, but flag it if 'remember last used' is preferred.) UI: a slider + type-in number, seconds, range 0.5-60, step 0.5, one decimal (matches slideshow::format_interval's '2.0s'), label e.g. 'Slideshow interval'; group it with the other playback / nav-feel timing prefs (start speed, ramp, max photos per second) in whatever tab those live in. DISCOVERABILITY is the main point: the help overlay (/) and the new View-menu Slideshow checkmark already surface the keys, but only Settings shows the actual number.

tasks.title: Real progress feedback while decompressing a large archive
tasks.description: Replace the uninformative indeterminate spinner shown while a large .7z decompresses with real, determinate progress (a percentage / entry count, ideally a progress bar). Today a big archive opens behind a generic 'Loading archive…' toast and the password path shows a jerky 'Checking…' spinner (owner, 2026-06-28) — neither conveys that work is happening or how much is left, so a multi-second/GB extract looks hung.
tasks.details: ROOT CAUSE: the 7z open is eager decode-to-RAM (pb-source SevenZSource, task #30) run as ONE opaque blocking call on a worker thread — App::begin_archive_open spawns a thread that calls load_seven_z(path, password) and the channel only ever carries the FINAL result (poll_archive_load just try_recv's a done/err). So the UI can only show an indeterminate affordance: a 'Loading archive…' toast (show_toast) for the background load, and the egui Password dialog's 'Checking…' ui.spinner() (dialog.rs set_checking / DialogKind::Password) during a password re-open + validation. The loading pie (hud::render_pie / tick_pie / push_pie) that the photo path uses ALSO only has FAKE progress — main.rs notes it 'eases asymptotically toward but never reaches' a cap because there's no true decode progress; that asymptotic ease is the 'jerky'/uninformative feel. GOAL: surface genuine progress for the long case (large-archive extract), and make the brief password 'Checking…' clearly a different, short state. PLAN: (1) INVESTIGATE whether sevenz-rust2 exposes a per-entry or byte-level streaming/callback decode API (decompress entry-by-entry, or a progress callback) — if so, have the worker emit incremental progress; if the crate only offers a one-shot decode, either decode entry-by-entry ourselves (the archive_probe example already iterates entries) or contribute/patch a callback. The pre-flight (seven_z_preflight / seven_z_projected_bytes) already computes the TOTAL projected bytes + entry count, so a percentage denominator is in hand even before decode starts. (2) CHANGE THE CHANNEL from sending only the final Result to sending a small enum, e.g. ArchiveProgress::Update { done_entries, total_entries, done_bytes, total_bytes } and ArchiveProgress::Done(Result) (keep the archive_gen supersede check). poll_archive_load drains updates each tick and updates the indicator. (3) UI: show a DETERMINATE readout — reuse the loading pie by feeding it the REAL fraction instead of the asymptotic ease (its render_pie already takes progress 0..=1), and/or use the new centered message layer (Renderer::set_message, added for the empty-state hint) to show 'Decompressing… 45% (120/279)'. A thin progress bar is also an option (new tiny HUD primitive). Pick one; the centered text + real pie is probably the lowest-LOC, most legible combo. (4) Keep the password 'Checking…' spinner as-is (it's a brief validation, genuinely indeterminate), but make sure the LONG decompress that follows a correct password also shows the determinate progress, not just the spinner. CONSTRAINTS: progress updates must stay OFF the event-loop hot path (worker thread sends, event loop only reads + rasterizes on change, like push_pie's change-gated re-upload); no per-frame heap churn. PRIVACY (#2): progress is transient RAM-only UI state — no disk writes, consistent with the existing archive viewing guarantee. ZIP is lazy/per-entry so it opens fast and doesn't need this; scope is the eager 7z path (and any future eager format).
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: a unit test for the progress-fraction math (done/total clamped to 0..=1; total 0 doesn't divide-by-zero; a superseded generation's updates are dropped). If entry-by-entry decode is added, a test that the running count reaches total_entries on success. Manual: open a multi-GB .7z and confirm a smooth, advancing percentage/bar (not an asymptotic or frozen spinner) that completes, then the first photo shows; open an encrypted large .7z and confirm 'Checking…' (brief) hands off to the determinate decompress progress after the correct password; confirm a tiny archive still opens effectively instantly without a distracting flash.

tasks.title: macOS: borderless speed-mode fullscreen should cover the menu bar
tasks.description: On macOS our custom "speed mode" fullscreen (the F / Alt+Enter / F11 toggle — App::toggle_fullscreen — which sizes a borderless, decoration-less window to the monitor in the SAME Space, with no native toggleFullScreen: Spaces swoosh) leaves the system menu bar visible on top of the image. Owner (2026-06-29) wants it to cover the menu bar too, so the speed mode is genuinely edge-to-edge as the viewer intends, while keeping the no-transition, same-Space behavior (distinct from the separate native Ctrl+Cmd+F fullscreen).
tasks.details: WHERE: App::toggle_fullscreen (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs) is cross-platform — on entering speed mode it does window.set_fullscreen(None) + set_decorations(false) + sizes the window to current_monitor position/size; on exit it restores decorations + windowed geometry. On macOS a borderless window sized to the screen does NOT hide the menu bar (the bar stays drawn on top / the window does not extend under it), unlike Windows where the borderless resize is already edge-to-edge. tasks.title: Fix: opening a large nested folder beachballs then crashes (synchronous, unbounded recursive scan on the event-loop thread)
tasks.description: Opening a deep/large nested directory tree on macOS shows the spinning pinwheel (beachball) and then crashes. Root cause is structural, not macOS-specific in the code: the recursive image scan runs SYNCHRONOUSLY on the winit event-loop (main) thread, and the walk is UNBOUNDED RECURSION with no symlink-cycle guard. The long scan starves the run loop (→ macOS 'application not responding' beachball), and a deeply nested tree — or a symlink/alias cycle (common on macOS) — overflows the main thread's stack, which Rust turns into an uncatchable abort (the same class of hard crash noted for deep RAW decoders in CLAUDE.md). This violates the project norm 'Never block the event loop' — decode/I/O are off-thread, but the directory scan is not. Reported 2026-06-30 (owner). FIXED 2026-06-30: the recursive walk is now iterative + symlink-non-following + error-tolerant + cancellable (walkdir, replacing the hand-rolled recursion in collect_recursive → collect_images), and folder scans run OFF the event-loop thread (begin_dir_scan/poll_dir_scan, mirroring the async 7z path: thread::spawn + mpsc + scan_gen generation counter + shared cancel flag; the current view stays put, a slow scan flashes a deferred 'Scanning folder…' toast). Unit tests added: recursive_scan_walks_nested_subfolders, recursive_scan_does_not_follow_symlink_cycle (the crash regression), scan_honors_cancel_flag; the no-trace privacy tests still pass (the off-thread scan is read-only). REMAINING (status review): on-device confirmation that opening ~/Library no longer beachballs/crashes; and the macos_open.rs TEMP DEBUG that writes opened paths to /tmp/pb_openurls_dbg.txt is NOT yet removed — left untouched to avoid colliding with the other agent working in the macOS files (still a privacy-guarantee violation + must-remove-before-commit).
tasks.details: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading the code): App::open_input (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs ~1650) → resolve_playlist → resolve_source (~4505) → scan_images (~4341) → collect_recursive (~4321) all run on the event-loop thread. open_input is called from about_to_wait (drops ~4077, macOS openURLs ~4086), resumed (deferred launch ~3803), and the file picker (~2469) — every entry point is the main thread. Two distinct failure modes: (1) BEACHBALL: collect_recursive does a synchronous std::fs::read_dir walk of the whole tree (plus paths.sort()) before the playlist exists; for a large tree this blocks winit's run loop for seconds, and macOS shows the spinning-wait cursor / can flag the app unresponsive. (2) CRASH: collect_recursive (main.rs:4321) recurses once per directory depth with NO depth cap and NO visited/symlink-cycle protection — a deeply nested tree exhausts the ~8 MB main-thread stack, and a directory symlink/alias that points at an ancestor recurses infinitely → guaranteed stack overflow → process abort (uncatchable; catch_unwind does not help, exactly like the NEF stack-overflow caveat). PRECEDENT FOR THE FIX: the .7z archive open already solved the same 'slow open must not freeze the loop' problem — begin_archive_open (~1683) does a RAM pre-flight then std::thread::spawn's the heavy work, shows a determinate progress + Cancel dialog (DialogWindow / OpenProgress), and picks up the result in poll_archive_load via a channel, bumping archive_gen so a superseded open is discarded. FIX DIRECTION: (a) make the walk iterative + safe — replace the recursive collect_recursive with an explicit work-queue (VecDeque) walk, OR adopt the `walkdir` crate (iterative, follow_links=false by default, has loop detection); either way add a hard depth cap and/or a visited-canonical-path set so symlink/alias cycles can't loop forever. (b) move the scan OFF the event-loop thread for the large case (thread::spawn like the 7z path) so the loop stays responsive and the existing loading/Cancel dialog can show progress, with a generation counter to drop superseded scans; the current photo (if any) stays on screen until the scan lands. (c) consider streaming/cap: surface results incrementally or cap absurd counts with a toast rather than allocating a giant Vec<PathBuf> up front. Keep the simple non-recursive path synchronous (it's cheap). This is cross-platform hardening; it just manifests first on macOS. NOTE while in here: macos_open.rs currently has a TEMP DEBUG `dbg()` that appends opened file paths to /tmp/pb_openurls_dbg.txt — that both must be removed before commit and is a privacy-guarantee violation (a persisted trace of viewed paths, task #2); kill it.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit (pure, in pb-core or a testable helper): extract the directory walk into a function that takes a depth cap + cycle guard and unit-test it against a synthesized temp tree — assert it (1) finds all supported images, (2) terminates on a symlink that points to an ancestor (build the cycle in the test, follow_links off or visited-set on), and (3) respects the depth cap. Property/regression: a deeply nested synthetic tree (e.g. 2000+ levels) completes without overflowing (proves the recursion→iteration change). Manual/on-device: open a large real nested tree on macOS and confirm no beachball (loop stays responsive / Cancel works) and no crash; confirm the no-trace integration test still passes (the off-thread scan must remain read-only — viewing_a_folder_writes_nothing_to_disk). Also confirm /tmp/pb_openurls_dbg.txt is no longer written.
